Some are family heads ('Sylviinæ.--', 'Anatidæ, Geese.--', 'Larinæ, Gulls.--') or bare group heads ('Swans.--' 1779, 'Ducks.--' 1784), and several species run on inside one paragraph. Punctuation varies: 'Stonechat, _P. rubicola_,--' (1285) and 'Shore Lark, _Otocorys alpestris_ (Linn.)--' (1622) lack the '.' before '--'. Some paragraphs have no head and continue the one before: 1379-1385 and 1383 (Goldcrest), 1710-1715 (Swift). Footnotes [5]-[8] sit between entries. Within entries 'Spring:' and 'Autumn:' mark the season. Heligoland (Gätke), Great Cotes, Spurn, Teesmouth, Yarmouth and the light stations are mixed in each entry; Heligoland has no separate section.

sections.note: Under each species there is one entry per station: '_Station._--dates...'. The species are bare headings on their own line, after two blank lines ('Eagle.' 3248 ... 'Stormy Petrel.' 4818). Some headings are quoted or compound: '"Goldfinch."' 3598, '"Bullfinch."' 3677, '"Kingfisher."' 3929, 'Golden and "Grey" Plover.' 3977, '"Sea Larks."' 4072. Under each species the spring entries come first, in Fastnet-round order, and then the run starts again for autumn. There is no season marker, so the season has to be read from the dates or the restart of the order. A station can appear twice under one species, once per season. Entries that run on mid-line: 'Rathlin Island.--Aug.' (3498) and 'Valentia.--Oct.' (3600). Entries without underscores: 'Dungarvan.--' (4112). '_Arklow Bank_, South,--' (3510) is malformed. 'Swallows.--June 22nd' (4689) is inside the Blacksod entry and is not a station. Variant names: 'Gaily Head' (3781, for Galley Head), 'Dursey Head' (4610), 'Kish Light-ship' (4558), 'Blackrock, Mayo' (4725) and 'Black Rock, Mayo', 'South Maidens Light' (3689). notes:
I read the whole report, lines 1-4851. The licence text after line 4851 I only skimmed far enough to place the boundary. The 28 sections run from line 1 to 5202 with no gaps or overlaps.

Points a cutting program should know:
(1) This year's Irish observations are grouped under bird names, but each entry starts with a station ('_Tuskar Rock._--Oct. 13th, ...'), so I called that part 'station'. Within each species the spring entries come first in station order, then the order restarts for autumn. Nothing in the text marks the change, so the season has to come from the dates.
(2) The two Scottish coasts use one paragraph per bird family ('Turdidæ.--'), with spring and autumn in the same paragraph. They were digested from the schedules and are the only place those records appear, so I marked them primary.
(3) East England is the only coast with a paragraph per species. Heligoland, Great Cotes and Spurn notes are mixed into it; Heligoland has no section of its own.
(4) The General Remarks for the East Coast of Scotland are printed under the West Coast of Scotland, at lines 2599-2912. Both General Remarks sections are marked summary, but each holds some records not printed elsewhere; the notes give the line ranges.
(5) Some sections are not lighthouse records: the Faroe paragraph (182-208), the Stevns (Denmark) table, and the moth note.
(6) No 1882 station list for the West Coast of England, Isle of Man or Wales is printed. The report says that part never arrived.
(7) Copy the four station lists with care. East Scotland starts at No. 4 and has '7B. Fair Isle', '(_a_)' and '"No birds."'. West Scotland has a Monach row with two heights, braced Nos. 93/94 and a wrapped No. 95. The Irish list uses No. 5 twice and wraps observer names onto continuation lines. East England has one row reading 'The Principal.' and rows with two keepers joined by '&'.
